back: An automatic check that input data is reasonable and follows set rules; it cannot prove the data is correct.
A check that data has been entered or copied accurately, matching the original (visual check, double entry).
Range: between limits. Length: number of characters. Type: correct data type. Presence: not blank. Format: pattern of characters.
An extra digit calculated from the other digits; recalculated on input to detect mistyped or swapped digits (ISBNs, bar codes).
Multiply the first 12 digits by 1, 3, 1, 3, …; add; check digit = (10 − total MOD 10) MOD 10.
Data is entered twice and the two entries are compared; accepted only if they match. Used for new passwords.
The user compares the data on screen with the source, or confirms data the program displays.
Prompt, INPUT, then REPEAT … UNTIL valid (or WHILE invalid DO) with an error message and re-input inside the loop.
A wrong value that is still sensible (e.g. 46 typed as 64) passes validation; verification is needed to catch it.
